title: Review: Giant covalent structures; Shapes of molecules (VSEPR); Oxidation states and naming; Oxidation states and half-equations
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: RX01#t4 term and clue written for the game; RX01#t3 term and clue written for the game; BD03#t2 term and clue written for the game; BD03#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: BD03#N.6, BD05#N.7, RX01#N.13, RX02#N.10, BD03#N.3a, BD05#N.11a, RX01#N.6a, RX02#N.8, BD03#N.9a, RX01#N.11a, RX02#N.4a, BD03#N.5a. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Reduction
items.clue: Gain of electrons, as when each O atom goes from 0 to −2 during rusting.

items.label: Reducing agent
items.clue: The reactant that gives electrons away, like Zn in Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu.

items.label: Expanded octet
items.clue: More than eight outer electrons on a central atom, possible from period 3 on.

items.label: VSEPR
items.clue: Model in which electron pairs around a central atom get as far apart as possible.

questions.stem: Which molecule has four electron pairs arranged tetrahedrally around its central atom, but a non-linear (bent) shape?

options.text: SO₂
CH₄
NH₃
H₂S

questions.explanation: S has two bonding pairs and two lone pairs, like O in water: tetrahedral arrangement, and the atoms H–S–H are bent.

questions.stem: Substance X melts at 1710 °C. It does not conduct electricity, either as a solid or when molten. It does not dissolve in water or in hexane. Which structure does X have?

options.text: A lattice of oppositely charged ions
A network of atoms joined by covalent bonds throughout
A lattice of metal cations in a sea of delocalised electrons
Separate small molecules with very strong forces between them

questions.explanation: The very high melting point means strong bonds break. No conduction even when molten means no ions and no delocalised electrons. Insoluble everywhere: a covalent network.

options.text: Cl₂ + 2KBr → 2KCl + Br₂
2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO
2H₂O₂ → 2H₂O + O₂
NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O

questions.explanation: O in H₂O₂ is −1 (a peroxide). It goes to −2 in H₂O (reduced) and to 0 in O₂ (oxidised): one element in one species, both ways.

questions.stem: Chlorine is −1 in the chloride ion, Cl⁻, but +1 in the hypochlorite ion, ClO⁻ (in bleach). Which explains the +1?

options.text: The chlorine atom in ClO⁻ has lost a proton to the oxygen atom, leaving chlorine with a +1 charge.
Oxygen always has the oxidation number −1 in an ion with one negative charge.
Oxygen is more electronegative than chlorine, so it is assigned the shared electrons in the Cl–O bond.
The chlorine atom in ClO⁻ carries a real charge of +1, as in a Cl⁺ ion.

questions.explanation: O takes both shared electrons and is −2; the total must be −1, so x + (−2) = −1 and Cl is +1. In Cl⁻, chlorine holds an extra electron: −1.

questions.stem: Ammonia, NH₃, has three bonding pairs and one lone pair around the nitrogen atom. What is its shape?

options.text: Tetrahedral, as there are four electron pairs around the nitrogen atom
Trigonal planar, as only the three bonding pairs repel one another
Flat, with 90° bond angles, as the atoms are drawn in its dot-and-cross diagram on paper
Pyramidal (trigonal pyramidal), as the lone pair occupies one of four tetrahedral positions

questions.explanation: Four pairs point to the corners of a tetrahedron. Atoms sit at three of them, so N is at the top of a pyramid: about 107°.

questions.stem: Graphite conducts electricity far better along its layers than at right angles to them. Which statement explains this?

options.text: Its layers slide over each other, and charge is carried only in the direction they slide.
Its ions lie between the layers, so they can move only in the plane of the layers.
Each atom forms four bonds within its layer, so no electrons are left to pass between layers.
Its delocalised electrons move freely within a layer, but cannot easily cross the gap to the next.

questions.explanation: Each C bonds to three others; its fourth electron is delocalised over its own layer only. So charge flows easily along a layer, but hardly between layers.

questions.stem: Chlorine reacts with aqueous iron(II) ions: 2Fe²⁺(aq) + Cl₂(aq) → 2Fe³⁺(aq) + 2Cl⁻(aq). Which species is the oxidising agent in this reaction?

options.text: Fe²⁺, since it loses electrons and so is itself oxidised
Cl₂, since it gains electrons and so is itself reduced
Cl⁻, since it is the species holding the gained electrons
None, since no species here gains or loses any oxygen atoms

questions.explanation: Chlorine's oxidation number falls from 0 to −1: each Cl₂ gains two electrons from Fe²⁺. The species that accepts electrons is the oxidising agent.

options.text: K₂Cr₂O₇, potassium dichromate(VI)
K₂MnO₄, potassium manganate(IV)
Fe₂(SO₄)₃, iron(VI) sulfate
MnCl₂, manganese(VII) chloride

questions.explanation: 2(+1) + 2x + 7(−2) = 0 gives 2x = +12, so each Cr is +6. The numeral is per atom.

questions.stem: In xenon tetrafluoride, XeF₄, the xenon atom (eight outer electrons) forms a single bond to each of four fluorine atoms. What is the shape of XeF₄?

options.text: Tetrahedral, as only its four bonding pairs repel one another around the Xe atom
Octahedral, as there are six electron pairs around the xenon atom
Square planar, as the two lone pairs occupy opposite positions of an octahedron
See-saw, as the two lone pairs occupy adjacent positions, 90° apart, in an octahedron

questions.explanation: 8 − 4 = 4 non-bonding electrons: two lone pairs. They sit 180° apart, leaving four F in a square plane.

questions.stem: In acidic solution, MnO₄⁻(aq) is reduced to Mn²⁺(aq) and Fe²⁺(aq) is oxidised to Fe³⁺(aq). In the balanced overall redox equation, what amount of Fe²⁺ reacts with 1 mol of MnO₄⁻?

options.text: 1 mol
5 mol
2 mol
3 mol

questions.explanation: Mn goes from +7 to +2, so each MnO₄⁻ gains 5 electrons; each Fe²⁺ loses 1. The iron half-equation is multiplied by 5.

questions.stem: What are the oxidation numbers of hydrogen in sodium hydride, NaH, and of oxygen in sodium peroxide, Na₂O₂?
questions.explanation: In NaH, Na is +1, so H is −1 (the hydride ion). In Na₂O₂, 2(+1) + 2x = 0, so O is −1 (the peroxide ion, O₂²⁻).

questions.stem: Predict the H–O–H bond angle in a water molecule, H₂O.

options.text: About 104.5°, as lone pairs repel more strongly than bonding pairs do
About 109.5°, as all four electron pairs around O repel one another equally
About 180°, as the two bonding pairs get as far apart as possible
About 90°, as the H atoms are drawn at right angles in its dot-and-cross diagram

questions.explanation: Two bonding pairs and two lone pairs, arranged tetrahedrally. The lone pairs repel more, squeezing the angle below 109.5°.
